validated_results.title: Alcohol consumption and risk of renal cell cancer: the NIH-AARP diet and health study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study reporting multivariate relative risks for alcohol consumption and incident renal cell cancer, with sex-specific estimates.

extraction.comparison_type: 30 g per day vs >0 to <5 g per day of alcohol consumption
extraction.timing: Prospective (exposure assessed at baseline before cancer diagnosis)
extraction.population: NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study participants

cases.excerpt: The relationship between alcohol consumption and RCC was examined in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study (n=49 2187, 1814 cases).

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with >0 to <5 g per day of alcohol consumption, the multivariate relative risk (95% confidence intervals) for 15 to <30 and 30 g per day was, 0.75 (0.63-0.90) and 0.71 (0.59-0.85), respectively, in men and 0.67 (0.42-1.07) and 0.43 (0.22-0.84), respectively, in women.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared with >0 to <5 g per day of alcohol consumption, the multivariate relative risk (95% confidence intervals) for 15 to <30 and 30 g per day was, 0.75 (0.63-0.90) and 0.71 (0.59-0.85), respectively, in men and 0.67 (0.42-1.07) and 0.43 (0.22-0.84), respectively, in women.
